title: Fix the Struct Pointer Member Access
description: The program should access a struct member through a pointer to that struct.
expectedBehavior: The program should print 3, the x member of the struct.
actualProblem: ptr is a pointer to a struct Point, not a struct Point itself, so the dot operator (.) doesn't apply to it — this is a compile error ('request for member x in something not a structure or union').
explanation: When accessing a struct's member through a pointer to that struct, C requires the arrow operator (->), which combines dereferencing the pointer and accessing the member in one step. The dot operator (.) is only valid on the struct value itself.
